architectureReason: main's history permanently contains 2052 generated .open-next/ blobs, ~25 of which carry developer machine paths, plus internal process, red-team, and agent-automation documents. A deterministic allowlist export is safer than repeated manual cleanup, and no history rewrite is authorized.
notes: This manifest is authoritative. docs/release/PUBLIC_REPOSITORY_INVENTORY.md is a generated human-readable projection of it.
Inclusion is allowlist-based: a tracked path is public only if it matches an `include` rule. Everything else is private by default.
Rules are evaluated in order; the FIRST matching rule wins. Every tracked path must match exactly one rule or verification fails as UNCLASSIFIED.
`trackedPathsDigest` pins the exact set of tracked paths. Adding or removing any tracked file changes it and fails verification until a human records a classification decision here.

forbiddenContent.allowReason: These two tests assert that absolute filesystem paths are REJECTED by the evidence guards. The literal is the negative fixture that proves the protection works; removing it would delete the proof.

forbiddenContent.reason: An unresolved placeholder must never reach a built artifact.
forbiddenContent.allowReason: wrangler.json is the committed safe TEMPLATE: the placeholders are the mechanism that keeps real D1 database ids out of Git. The operations docs instruct operators to replace them. The boundary manifest, this policy, and the listed tests name the literal because they DESCRIBE or ASSERT ON that mechanism; none is a built or deployed artifact.

publicationBlockers.detail: scripts/alpha-safety-gate.mjs (npm run alpha:safety-gate, a required CI Safety Gate step) reads internal release-governance artifacts that the boundary keeps private, including docs/release/ALPHA_RELEASE_MATRIX.json and docs/PHASE_7A_ALPHA_RELEASE_SAFETY_CHECKLIST.md. The gate therefore cannot pass in the public export as currently wired.
remediationOptions: Give the public mirror a reduced npm script set that omits alpha:safety-gate and the ratchet entries naming private tests.
Split the safety gate into a public product-invariant gate and a private release-governance gate.
Publish a redacted subset of the governance artifacts the gate reads.
publicationBlockers.requiredOwner: Product/release owner — this is a product configuration decision, deliberately not made inside the repository-boundary WorkUnit.

publicationBlockers.detail: package.json `test:canonical-pipeline-ratchets` explicitly names tests/architectureBoundaries.test.mts, which reads the SENSITIVE docs/architecture/CANONICAL_WORKUNIT_PIPELINE_REFACTOR_PROGRAM.md (a live list of open CSRF/auth/SSRF gaps). The named test is private, so the script entry dangles in the export.
remediationOptions: Split the ratchet into public-invariant and private-governance halves.
